sections.h2: Paying the bill and finding the right office
sections.html:
Billing and collecting belong to the Chattooga Tax Commissioner, who cannot change a value or a millage rate. Appraisals and exemption approvals come from the Board of Tax Assessors, whom the county commissioner appoints. Appeals are heard by a Board of Equalization picked by the Grand Jury. County tax rates come from the county commissioner, and school rates from the Board of Education.

  • Location: Courthouse Annex, 120 Cox Street, Summerville, GA 30747. Mail: P.O. Box 517, Summerville, GA 30747-0517.
  • Phone 706-857-0703. Hours run 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday, but the doors stay shut on Wednesdays.
  • You can look up and pay a bill at chattoogacountytax.com.
  • A mailed payment is accepted with a USPS postmark, not a metered one.

The bill is mailed to the homeowner and only sometimes to the lender. With an escrow account, forward your copy to the mortgage company.

Chattooga sits in Georgia's northwest corner, with 314 square miles and Summerville as the seat. Trion, Lyerly and Menlo are the other cities. Several county properties are on national historic registers, which can matter because Georgia offers preferential assessment for qualifying historic buildings.

Estimated population in 2025 was 25,300, close to the 24,965 counted in 2020. Homes held by their owners make up 66.8% of the total, with a median value of $115,600 for 2020 to 2024 and rent around $790. Just 2 building permits were issued in 2025.

Land, buildings and business equipment are normally due December 1. Interest starts accruing on December 2, and 120 days later a 5% penalty is added, though a homesteaded parcel owing less than $500 escapes that penalty. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1 and pick up 1% interest for each month of delay.

A levy on the property is possible for unpaid taxes, though the Tax Commissioner treats it as a last resort. A bill more than 30 days late can be recorded as a tax FiFa (lien) at the Superior Court clerk's office. These records are public and credit bureaus may read them, which the tax office cannot prevent.

Excess funds from past tax sales are listed on the Tax Commissioner's website, so a former owner can check whether money is waiting.

The Tax Commissioner lists both state exemptions and local ones that take the place of the state amount when they are bigger. Owning and living in the home on January 1 is required, and applications go to the Tax Assessor's Office. Filing is open year-round, yet only an application received by April 1 applies to that year.

Chattooga County homestead exemptions
ExemptionEligibilityBenefit
StandardAny qualifying homeowner$2,000 off the 40% assessed value; excludes bond levies
Standard elderly schoolAge 62 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $10,000 off assessed value, school tax only
Standard elderly generalAge 65 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $4,000 off assessed value for county, school and state
Local countyAge 70 or older, federal adjusted gross income at most $20,000Sliding 20% to 100% share of assessed value, county tax only, for the residence and up to 5 acres
Local schoolAge 70 or older, same income limitUp to $40,000 of assessed value, school tax only
FloatingAge 62 or older, household income at most $30,000State and county tax, not school; replaces other exemptions

Be careful with the floating exemption: it may raise a bill at first because it replaces other state and county exemptions. Owners with a service-connected disability qualify for a separate exemption, as do unremarried widows of service members killed in armed conflict and of firefighters or peace officers who died on duty.

A homestead owner age 62 or older, with gross household income up to $15,000, may defer tax but never erase it. Repayment generally comes due once ownership changes or the deferred taxes plus interest reach 85% of fair market value, so a sale usually triggers repayment from proceeds.

  • Land in genuine farming can be assessed at 30% rather than 40%, and conservation use property is valued as currently used. A covenant promising at least 10 years of that use is required for both.
  • Qualifying historic buildings may get preferential assessment covering the structure and as many as two surrounding acres.
  • Manufacturers may claim the Freeport exemption for raw goods, work in process and finished goods awaiting out-of-state shipment, applying to the Board of Tax Assessors from January 1 to April 1.

sections.h2: How to contest a Chattooga County value
sections.html:
Counting from the notice date, you have 45 days. The assessors get the appeal first and take a second look at their value. After that, the case can go to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a last written notice filed with the assessors moves it on to Superior Court.

You may contest taxability, value, or uniformity against neighboring properties. Saying the tax is too high will not work, because the county commissioner and Board of Education set that rate. A mobile home owner disputing a revised value has 30 days to get to the Board of Equalization.

Returns are accepted until April 1. After a first return, real property returns carry forward unless something changes, but personal property returns are needed every year.

The person who owns the property on January 1 owes the whole year, and part-year owners get no refund. Let the closing attorney divide the year on the settlement statement.

Your exemption does not transfer, so a purchaser moving in must file by April 1. For a deed copy for the closing file, visit the deed room kept by the Clerk of Superior Court in the Chattooga County Courthouse. With a median home value of $115,600, even a modest unpaid balance and penalty can weigh on a sale, so request a payoff early.

The tax office is closed Wednesdays, so schedule calls and visits for the other weekdays or check the bill online. Request a written payoff and find out whether any older year is open. A mobile or manufactured home has its own April 1 account, separate from the December bill, so check that one on its own.

Hand the payoff to the closing attorney early. Cash buyers want the same documents as anyone else, and a clean payoff keeps a lien from slowing the sale. Remember also that the buyer, not you, will file for a new homestead exemption after closing, so mention the April 1 date to them. If you inherited the house or are selling for an estate, ask the closing attorney about how the January 1 owner rule applies before the deed is signed.

faqs.q: What is the usual Chattooga County deadline?
faqs.a: Land, buildings and business equipment are due December 1. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Chattooga tax office on a Wednesday?
faqs.a: No, Wednesday is the closed day. On the other weekdays the office runs from 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM.

faqs.q: How costly is a late payment in Chattooga County?
faqs.a: Interest begins on the following day. After 120 days a 5% penalty is added, unless the property is homesteaded and the liability is under $500.

faqs.q: Does a Chattooga County homestead exemption need yearly renewal?
faqs.a: No. Once granted it renews automatically unless you move, change ownership or want a different exemption, and the deadline for a first application is April 1.

faqs.q: How do I find a deed copy for a Chattooga County property?
faqs.a: Go to the Superior Court clerk's deed room in the Chattooga County Courthouse.
